lens: CLAIMS AND SOURCES. I checked about 50 factual claims in DOSSIER.md against primary sources on 2026-10-15. Sources: HF API metadata and file trees summed with curl; full text of arXiv 2510.13999, 2610.02241, 2505.02390, 2509.25689, 2609.18110, 2608.12103, 2606.10493, 2608.18261, 2607.09686, 2406.11235, 2610.15417 and 2608.02989 via orx; WebFetch of model cards, the ds4 docs and the benchmark pages. Most numbers match their sources exactly; the list below excludes the claims that held. Confirmed: Apple 614 GB/s with 128 GB only on the 40-core M5 Max; K2-Thinking 594.3 GB and K2.6 595.3 GB; the K2 config arithmetic; Unsloth K2.6 PPL 2.4131 vs 1.8420; every ubergarm PPL ratio (+0.26%, +2.4%, +7.8%, +24.8%, +34.7%, +43.0%); Unsloth K2 sizes 246.8, 248.6, 340.5 and 383.6 GB; ds4 M5 Max 39.35/790.18, 34.36/557.04 and 27.64/398.50; AA v4.3.2 scores 34, 27 and 12; LM Studio #2040 105/1,833; oMLX 79.7/41.4/14.0; Awni's 15 tok/s on 2x M3 Ultra; Simon Willison's ~1.7 tok/s; the REAP K2 table (0.631 to 0.624, 0.554 to 0.576, 0.355 to 0.164, 0.780 to 0.643); MoESQ 80.77 vs 82.43 (97.99%) and GSQ 94.22%; China Unicom -0.68%, -1.80%, -0.94%, -0.34%, -8.91%, -14.66% and 2.70 bits; Aider V3.1 table; RedHat 99.82%; KTransformers 10-14 tok/s at about 600 GB; OSDI'26 K2 FP8 22.4 tok/s on 1.15 TB + 2x RTX 5090; Geerling 20.21/168.90 and 14.82/86.09; MacStories 24 vs 16; someoddcodeguy 8,296 MiB and 189/11; Weschera 80.8 GiB, 97.15 GiB and 8.39 GiB; SSD-LLaMA 77.7%, 4.1x, 19.7 GiB and K3 0.465/1.217; trace-study locality and LRU numbers; flash-moe 4.36 tok/s with K=4; Unsloth K3 sizes and fidelity; licences for K2.6, V4, GLM, Qwen3.5 and Mistral Large 3.

problems.claim: Sec 2 lines 275 and 313: ds4 has an SSD-streaming mode 'but the text the sweeps read gave no speeds [S95]'; no streamer is documented for these models on Metal. Sec 2 line 145: GLM-5.3 is among the models that 'do not fit 128 GB at any published size'. Sec 1: 'Kimi-class models cannot be made to fit this Mac with usable quality and speed.'
problems.problem: Superseded and omitted. The ds4 maintainer published streaming measurements on exactly this hardware (128 GB M5 Max) on 2026-09-06, five weeks before the dossier. They include a ~753B open model (full GLM 5.3) running from SSD. The dossier says these numbers do not exist. This changes the answer to Kevin's actual question about 700B-class local models, and it supplies the Metal streaming calibration the dossier calls missing (gap G2 and the section 3b prefill estimate).
problems.evidence: https://github.com/antirez/ds4/blob/main/docs/SSD_STREAMING.md (read in full via raw.githubusercontent; commits dated 2026-09-05 and 2026-09-06 per the GitHub API). Section 'M5 Max measurements' (128 GB M5 Max, automatic cache, no speculative decoding): (1) GLM 5.3 Flash Q4_K, 177.77 GiB: prefill 121 t/s initial and 104 t/s continued; generation 11.9 / 14.9 t/s; three-run median; 2K prompt + 1K append. (2) DeepSeek Flash Vision Exp MXFP4, 145.26 GiB (native-precision experts): prefill 300 / 263 t/s; generation 11.9 / 19.3 t/s; single run; 8K prompt + 4K append; 86.2 GiB expert cache. (3) 'Full GLM 5.3 IQ2_XXS (196.58 GiB) ... generation afterward rose from 4.09 to 5.11 t/s' (8K context, 61.35 GiB cache, three-run medians, 64 tokens). HF API: zai-org/GLM-5.3 has 753,329,940,480 parameters and licence 'glm-5.3'.
problems.fix: Add a 'streamed on this Mac (maintainer-measured)' block to sections 1, 2 and 3(b) with these three rows, labelled maintainer measurement with workload caveats ('workload references, not a speed guarantee'; generation includes first-token wait). Add a feasibility row for full GLM 5.3 IQ2_XXS (211 GB file, fits on disk after the Trash). Reword the short answer: Kimi itself has no measured Metal path, but a ~750B open model streams at ~4-5 tok/s on this Mac. Recalibrate A6 and the prefill estimate against the 121-300 t/s measured prefill.

problems.claim: Row D4: the pruned DeepSeek V3-0324 file is '103 GB (508B parameters, 1.62 bits average). A 130 GB variant also exists.' Fit: 'Tight. 95.9 GiB + 4 GiB KV at 32K + buffers ≈ 103 GiB.' Quality: 'The 130 GB version scores Winogrande 77.63, MMLU 84.55...'. Sec 3(c): this pruned GGUF is listed as a ready-made file.
problems.problem: Wrong file size and wrong fit verdict. The only published pruned file is 105.58 GiB (113.4 GB, 1.79 BPW), not 103 GB. With the dossier's own 4 GiB of KV at 32K and 3 GiB of buffers, it comes to about 112.6 GiB, above the 107.5 GiB ceiling, so the label should be 'No', not 'Tight'. The '130 GB variant' is also misattributed. In the paper's Table 1 it is mixed precision applied to the full-size, unpruned DeepSeek-V3. Its benchmark scores therefore do not describe a pruned model.
problems.evidence: arXiv 2509.25689 (read in full via orx): Table 1 caption 'Benchmark results of full-seized DeepSeek-V3(671B) between ours mixed precision optimized version and 2 baseline quant'; row 'Ours (Mixed) 130GB 77.63 84.55 86.08 84.58 93.56'. The pruned 103 GB model appears only in Fig. 3 against IQ1_M 140 GB. HF moxin-org/DeepSeek-V3-0324-Moxin-GGUF README (read in full, 2026-10-15): 'For our smallest compressed version 105.58 GiB (1.79 BPW)'. The V3-Mini-Exp folder sums to 113.4 GB (4 shards, HF API).
problems.fix: Change D4 to file 113.4 GB / 105.6 GiB and fit 'No' (or 'Tight only with ~1K context and a raised wired limit'). Drop the claim that a pruned 130 GB variant exists. Move the 130 GB scores to an 'unpruned mixed-precision' note. State that the pruned model has figure-only comparisons.

problems.claim: Sec 5 'Other host constraints': 'The kwanhee pruned Kimi needs its author's vLLM fork, a published fork that would need its own pinned image [S64].' Row K4: 'It needs the author's vLLM fork'.
problems.problem: The fork is not public. The model card names 'kwanhee-lee/vllm-private', branch 'paired48-nvfp4-moe', and that repository returns 404. The 288 GB REAP-50 Kimi, the dossier's best measured prune-plus-quantize point, therefore cannot be run on the H100 host with any published runtime.
problems.evidence: HF kwanhee/Kimi-K2.5-REAP50-INT4-W4A16 card (WebFetch, 2026-10-15): runtime is the 'kwanhee-lee/vllm-private' fork, branch 'paired48-nvfp4-moe'; stock vLLM fails to load it. curl https://github.com/kwanhee-lee/vllm-private gives HTTP 404; GitHub API gives 'Not Found' (2026-10-15).
problems.fix: Replace 'a published fork' with 'a private fork (404 as of 2026-10-15); not runnable without the author's help'. Mark G1's reuse of this checkpoint as blocked unless the fork is released.

problems.claim: Sec 3(c) Limits: 'No GGUF or MLX pruned Kimi exists.' Sec 1 item 3: 'Nobody has published a general-purpose Kimi with more than 50% of its experts removed.' G1 rests partly on this.
problems.problem: False for the Kimi family. Community REAP-pruned Kimi K3 builds exist in MLX and GGUF, including 80-82% expert removal with a mixed general-domain calibration. They report qualitative failures, which is direct prior evidence for G1. A K2.5 REAP build in safetensors also exists.
problems.evidence: HF API, 2026-10-15: mlx-community/Kimi-K3-mlx-reap160-2bit (181.2 GB; card: 160 of 896 experts kept, 82% pruned; 'Factual recall ... failing'; decode 3.93 tok/s on CUDA). pipenetwork/Kimi-K3-REAP80-MLX-mxfp4-q8 (~350 GB; 179 of 896 kept; calibration '40% code ... 30% English web, 15% Chinese...'; 5.54 tok/s on a 512 GiB M3 Ultra; 'Expect noticeable degradation versus full K3'). prometheusAIR/Kimi-K3-REAP55-GGUF (342.5 GB). mmnga-o/Kimi-K3-REAP50-UD-gguf. Ex0bit/Kimi-K2.5-PRISM-REAP-530B-A32B (309.7 GB). Cards skimmed via WebFetch.
problems.fix: Reword to: 'No pruned Kimi K2.x exists in GGUF or MLX. Community K3 builds pruned 50-82% exist in MLX and GGUF, with qualitative reports of failed factual recall and no benchmarks.' Cite them, label them community reports, and add them to G1's 'why it is open' as prior negative evidence.

problems.claim: Sec 1 item 2: 'The smallest Kimi K2 file anyone publishes is 247-249 GB. That is Unsloth's 1.8-bit build [S16].'
problems.problem: Wrong, and it contradicts the dossier's own row K3, which lists ubergarm builds of 251 GB and 236 GB. Smaller K2-family files are published, including one for K2.6.
problems.evidence: HF API file-size sums (2026-10-15): ubergarm smol-IQ1_KT is 235.1 GB (218.9 GiB) for each of Kimi-K2-Instruct-0905, K2-Thinking, K2.5 and K2.6. unsloth/Kimi-K2.5-GGUF UD-TQ1_0 is 239.5 GB (223.1 GiB). Unsloth's K2 guide lists K2-Instruct UD-TQ1_0 at 245 GB.
problems.fix: Change to: 'The smallest published K2-family files are about 235 GB (ubergarm smol-IQ1_KT, 1.84 bits, +43% PPL on K2; needs ik_llama.cpp) and 239.5 GB (Unsloth K2.5 UD-TQ1_0).'

problems.claim: Sec 1 and row F1: DeepSeek V4 Flash 'at full precision ... scores 34 on the Artificial Analysis index' [S105]. Row F1 fidelity is +34% PPL and 78.15% top-1 for the 'likely same file' [S23]. Row F2 uses UD-IQ3_XXS at 103.0 GB. G4 compares ds4 Q2 with Unsloth quants and the 'official FP4/FP8 weights'.
problems.problem: The dossier never separates DeepSeek V4 Flash checkpoint revisions, and newer ones supersede it. The AA score of 34 is for 'DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 (Max)', a later re-post-trained checkpoint run at the max reasoning setting. The ds4f-q2 download is built from 0731. The 103.0 GB IQ3_XXS file and (most likely) the Unsloth fidelity table come from the April checkpoint repo; 0731 has its own files, e.g. IQ3_XXS at 104.2 GB. antirez publishes same-size IQ2XXS files for the April checkpoint, for 0731 and for Vision-Exp. 'Likely the same file' is therefore unresolved, and G4 as written would confound checkpoint with quantization. The newer DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, released 2026-09-10 under MIT with AA score 39 (above 34), is missing from the feasibility table.
problems.evidence: https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/comparisons/deepseek-v4-flash-vs-kimi-k2-6 (WebFetch 2026-10-15): 'DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 (Max): 34', index v4.3.2. https://github.com/antirez/ds4/blob/main/docs/MODELS.md: ds4f-q2 '~81 GiB', base checkpoint 'DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731'. HF API: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash created 2026-04-22; deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 created 2026-07-31 (304.2B incl. DSpark); unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF UD-IQ3_XXS 104.2 GB vs unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-GGUF UD-IQ3_XXS 103.0 GB. antirez/deepseek-v4-gguf has three 86.72 GB IQ2XXS files (April, April imatrix, -0731). https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/deepseek-v4-1-flash: score 39, 552B total / 16B active, released 2026-09-10.
problems.fix: Name the checkpoint everywhere ('V4 Flash 0731', 'max reasoning' for the AA score). Point F2 and the host download list at the 0731 files. Mark the S23 fidelity metrics as 'checkpoint unconfirmed'. In G4, quantize the same checkpoint as the reference. Add a V4.1 Flash row (streaming-only on one 128 GB Mac per ds4 MODELS.md).

problems.claim: Sec 3(b) recipe step 3: 'if a model larger than RAM is wanted, try ds4's streaming mode with V4.1 Flash Q2 first.' Sec 5: about 358 GB will be free after the Trash is emptied.
problems.problem: Infeasible by the dossier's own disk numbers. The ds4 V4.1 Flash Q2 download is a single 341 GiB file (366 GB, mostly Engram tables), which is larger than the 358 GB the dossier expects to be free. ds4 also publishes no V4.1 Flash speed, whereas measured streaming targets that fit on disk do exist (see the blocker above).
problems.evidence: https://github.com/antirez/ds4/blob/main/docs/MODELS.md (WebFetch 2026-10-15): 'ds41f-q2 | 341 GiB file; 152 GiB main weights | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | 189 GiB Engram tables; one 128 GB Mac uses SSD streaming'. SSD_STREAMING.md gives no V4.1 Flash speed.
problems.fix: Replace the recommendation with the measured streaming targets that fit on disk: DeepSeek Flash MXFP4 (145 GiB = 156 GB), GLM 5.3 Flash Q4_K (177.8 GiB = 191 GB), full GLM 5.3 IQ2_XXS (196.6 GiB = 211 GB). Mark V4.1 Flash Q2 as 'needs ~366 GB of disk; unmeasured'.

problems.claim: A5: 'Streaming engines reach between 43% of sequential bandwidth (llama.cpp mmap of a GGUF file) and 78% (SSD-LLaMA's expert-pack layout) [S36].' Sec 3(b) Limits: 'llama.cpp mmap reaches at most 43% of the SSD's bandwidth [S36].'
problems.problem: Misattributed. SSD-LLaMA says 43.2% is the 'best-performing baseline' without naming it. The same paragraph reports speedups of up to 2.82x over llama.cpp and 1.93x over KTransformers. Since 77.7/43.2 = 1.80, the 43.2% baseline is most likely KTransformers, which would put llama.cpp mmap nearer ~28%. The paper also says Colibri reaches slightly higher bandwidth than SSD-LLaMA on some models, so 78% is not a ceiling. All figures are from a Linux PC with a 9 GiB/s NVMe, not macOS.
problems.evidence: arXiv 2609.18110 sec 5.2 (read in full via orx): 'SSD-LLaMA achieves up to 77.7% of the peak SSD sequential read bandwidth (9 GiB/s on our testbed), whereas the best-performing baseline only reaches 43.2% (3.89 GiB/s)'; 'up to 2.82× and 1.93× speedups over llama.cpp and KTransformer'; 'Colibri achieves slightly higher read bandwidth than SSD-LLaMA on some models'.
problems.fix: Reword: '43% for the best baseline (unnamed, likely KTransformers); llama.cpp mmap is lower, up to 2.8x below SSD-LLaMA; Linux/CUDA testbed'. Widen the stock-mmap lower bound (e.g. about 3.7 GB/s, 27% of 13.6) or label 5.85 GB/s as a purpose-built-streamer floor.

problems.claim: Sec 5 H100 host: Kimi K2.6 INT4 (595 GB) on 8x H100 'leaves about 45 GB in total, about 5.6 GB per GPU'. By A9, a 64K sequence needs about 8.1 GiB of MLA cache. G1 and G5 risks rest on this.
problems.problem: Unit error and wrong KV layout. An '80 GB' H100 exposes 81,559 MiB (about 85.5 GB), so 8 GPUs give about 684 GB and leave about 89 GB (about 11 GB per GPU) before runtime overhead, not 45 GB. The 8.1 GiB figure comes from llama.cpp's (512+64+512)-value layout, whereas vLLM caches 576 latent values per layer per token, about 4.3 GiB at 64K. The risk assessment is therefore about 2x too pessimistic.
problems.evidence: Dossier's own convention: 'GB = 10^9 bytes'. H100 SXM 80 GB total memory as reported by nvidia-smi is 81,559 MiB (standard figure; not re-measured on the host in this check; verify with nvidia-smi on the host). Kimi K2 config.json (fetched): kv_lora_rank 512, qk_rope_head_dim 64, 61 layers, so 576 × 61 × 2 bytes = 70,272 bytes per token.
problems.fix: Measure free HBM with nvidia-smi on the host and restate the headroom in one unit. Give KV per runtime: llama.cpp ~132.7 KB/token; vLLM MLA ~70.3 KB/token, replicated per TP rank.

problems.claim: Row Q1/F1 and conflict #9: 'community report: 33 / 28 at 128 / 8K context, reported at 103 GB with the quant not stated [S96]'; 'On an M5 Max running Qwen3.6, llama.cpp is 10-24% faster [S96].'
problems.problem: The quant is stated, and the speed gap is overstated. The source labels the V4 Flash row 'ds4 (q2–q4, 91 GB)', a different, larger mix than the 80.8 GiB Q2 file in row F1, and its decode figures include reasoning tokens. The +24% llama.cpp advantage is the 35B-A3B MoE with MTP; without MTP it is about +10%, and the dense 27B shows 0-6%.
problems.evidence: https://github.com/stared/benching-local-llms-on-apple-silicon (WebFetch 2026-10-15; run dated 2026-06-14): 'ds4 (q2–q4, 91 GB)', memory 103 GB, 'decode = total tok/s (reasoning included)'. 35B-A3B: 105 (llama.cpp+MTP) vs 85 (MLX); 93 vs 85 without MTP. 27B: 18 vs 17.
problems.fix: Say 'ds4 q2-q4 mix, 91 GB file, 103 GB in use; decode includes reasoning tokens'. Restate the MLX vs llama.cpp gap as '+9-10% without MTP and +24% with MTP on 35B-A3B; ~0-6% on dense 27B'.

problems.claim: Sec 3(e): 'Two M5 Max laptops over Thunderbolt 5 with ds4 ran V4 Flash Q4 at 25.1 tokens/s, with 1.38-1.85× faster prefill [S100].'
problems.problem: Partly unsupported. The page lists 25.1 t/s under link quality ('Thunderbolt 5 25.1 t/s · WiFi 10.7 t/s · Internet / VPN 3.6 t/s') and does not explicitly call it Q4 decode. It also says generation 'pays roughly a 19% penalty over a single machine'. The prefill speedups are confirmed: 1.38x, 1.66x and 1.85x at 9.4K, 28.7K and 63.8K tokens.
problems.evidence: https://dwarfstar.sh/benchmarks/ (WebFetch 2026-10-15; site built 2026-09-17).
problems.fix: Quote the figure as listed ('25.1 t/s over Thunderbolt 5, link-quality table') and add the 19% generation penalty.

problems.claim: Row O1 and sec 3(a): 'llama.cpp b9592 decode (tg128) 105, prefill (pp2048) 1,833 with the Metal 4 tensor API. LM Studio's bundled runtime gives 877 prefill [S97].'
problems.problem: 877 t/s is llama-bench with the tensor API disabled, which the poster says approximates LM Studio; it is not LM Studio's measured prefill. The page also does not confirm b9592 as the build behind these numbers; it cites b9592 only as a binary that logs 'has tensor = true'.
problems.evidence: https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lmstudio-bug-tracker/issues/2040 (WebFetch 2026-10-15): pp2048 877 (tensor API off) vs 1,833 (on); tg128 104.9 vs 105.1; 128 GB M5 Max, 40-core GPU, macOS 26.5; opened 2026-06-11 by oooseun.
problems.fix: Write: 'llama-bench with the tensor API off gives 877, which approximates LM Studio's runtime (community report; build not stated)'.

problems.claim: Sec 3(a): 'Kimi's tool-call schema accuracy ranges from 83% to 100% across serving providers, because of engine and parser differences, not bit width [S35].'
problems.problem: The source does not support the causal clause. It gives three possible causes: incorrect versions, malformed tool-call IDs, and no built-in JSON-schema enforcement. It does not rule out quantization. The 83-100% range holds only for kimi-k2-thinking; kimi-k2-0905 spans 71.96-100%.
problems.evidence: https://github.com/MoonshotAI/K2-Vendor-Verifier (WebFetch 2026-10-15; test date 2025-11-15): K2-thinking schema_accuracy 83.05% (Chutes) to 100%; K2-0905 71.96% (Together) to 100%; 'Some vendors may not meet the requirements due to using incorrect versions.'
problems.fix: Drop 'not bit width'. Write '83-100% (K2-Thinking) and 72-100% (K2-0905) across providers; causes cited are versions, ID formats and lack of schema enforcement'.

problems.claim: Row K1: 'measured: 0.89-1.03 streamed, Kimi-K2.7-Code Q4_0 on an RTX 5090 + 32 GB RAM + 9 GiB/s SSD [S36, paper]'.
problems.problem: The two numbers come from different RAM configurations: 0.89 tok/s is the default 16 GB testbed (MMLU), and 1.03 tok/s is with 32 GB.
problems.evidence: arXiv 2609.18110 sec 5.1 testbed: '16 GB of host DRAM ... up to 9 GiB/s'; sec 5.4: 'SSD-LLaMA achieves 1.03 tokens/s on the RTX 5090 + 32GB RAM configuration'; Fig. 10 shows 0.89 at the default configuration.
problems.fix: Write '0.89 (16 GB RAM) to 1.03 (32 GB RAM)'.

problems.claim: Sec 3(b): 'llama.cpp's new GPU LRU expert cache reached 77-89% hits and 1.6-2.2× faster decode [S41].'
problems.problem: Range truncated and scope omitted. The PR reports 72-89% hits and 1.57-2.20x. It runs on CUDA (RTX 4090/5090 hosts), is limited to batches of 32 tokens or fewer on a single device, and later comments report no gain on HIP or PCIe 3.0. Nothing shows it applies to Metal.
problems.evidence: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29887 (WebFetch 2026-10-15; merged 2026-10-07): Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q4_0; RTX 4090 72%/1.57x and 77%/1.62x; RTX 5090 77%/1.77x and 89%/2.20x.
problems.fix: State '72-89%, 1.57-2.20x, CUDA only, batch ≤32, single device; not shown on Metal'.

problems.claim: Row K4 and sec 3(c): MoESQ [S63] is 'an independent group'; the GPQA-Diamond 88.0%, AIME25 95.1% and MATH500 101.5% figures are cited as [S63, S64; independent paper].
problems.problem: S63 and S64 are not independent of each other. The MoESQ first author (Kwanhee Lee, POSTECH & ISTA, with Dan Alistarh) is the 'kwanhee' who uploaded the checkpoint. MoESQ's paper tables give only the OpenLLM v1 results for REAP-50+INT4; the GPQA, AIME and MATH500 recoveries appear only on the model card. MoESQ is independent of REAP's authors (Cerebras), not of the checkpoint.
problems.evidence: arXiv 2610.02241 (read in full via orx): authors Kwanhee Lee, Namhoon Lee, Dan Alistarh; Table 3/6 REAP 2.25 bits, 80.77, 97.99%. HF kwanhee/Kimi-K2.5-REAP50-INT4-W4A16 card: GPQA 0.7879 vs 0.8949 (88.0%), AIME25 0.9100 vs 0.9567, MATH500 0.9784 vs 0.9636.
problems.fix: Attribute the reasoning recoveries to the model card only and note that the paper and checkpoint share an author. Keep 'independent of the REAP authors'.

problems.claim: Row G1: 'the active-parameter count is not in the sweeps ... A = 20-40B as an unverified bracket'. Row G1: 'GLM-4.6 files are not listed in the sweeps.'
problems.problem: Both are resolvable. GLM-4.6 is widely reported as ~355B total / 32B active (same architecture as GLM-4.5), and Unsloth publishes GLM-4.6 GGUFs, e.g. UD-TQ1_0 at 84.1 GB.
problems.evidence: HF API unsloth/GLM-4.6-GGUF: GLM-4.6-UD-TQ1_0.gguf 84.1 GB. zai-org/GLM-4.6 has 356.8B safetensors parameters and an MIT licence. The card does not state the active count; secondary sources (web search 2026-10-15) agree on 32B active. GLM-4.5 tech report not opened in this check.
problems.fix: Use A = 32B (cite the GLM-4.5 report) to give ~28-37 tok/s at 1.89 bits, and list the GLM-4.6 files.

problems.claim: Sec 3(b): 'The bandwidth model holds. A pre-registered study found SSD decode bandwidth-bound and predictable from bytes ÷ bandwidth [S86].'
problems.problem: Overstated. The pre-registration covers that paper's router-training experiment, not the bandwidth measurement. The measurement contradicts itself: 0.44 tok/s warm × 12 GB/token = 5.3 GB/s, while the paper claims this 'recovers ~2.4 GB/s'; the model predicts 0.20 tok/s cold against a measured 0.128. The dossier flags this inconsistency in conflict #11 but still cites the study as proof that the model holds.
problems.evidence: arXiv 2608.18261 (read in full via orx): 'Decode is 0.44 tok/s warm; dividing the 12 GB/token read by the measured rate recovers ∼2.4 GB/s'; Table 2 decode cold 0.128 (model 0.20); prefill 0.25 tok/s; title 'A Pre-Registered Negative Result, with a Systems Measurement Study'.
problems.fix: Drop 'pre-registered' from this claim and cite it as weak, internally inconsistent support. Use the ds4 M5 Max streaming measurements as the calibration instead.

problems.claim: Sec 3(c): 'Pruning beats very low bits below 4 bits. On Qwen3-30B at 12.5% of BF16 size, EvalPlus scored 77.6 for 4-bit weights + 50% pruning vs 28.6 for 2-bit weights [S59].'
problems.problem: Numbers correct, generalisation not. The paper calls this a 'preliminary analysis' on one 30B model, with uniform AWQ W2A16-G128 as the 2-bit arm (not dynamic or trellis 2-bit), and states that 'weight quantization offers superior accuracy at a given compression ratio down to 4-bits'. The table even lists the 2-bit row with 64 experts, probably a typo.
problems.evidence: arXiv 2510.13999 Appendix E, Table A5 (read in full via orx): W4A16-G128, 64 experts, 12.5%, 77.6; W2A16-G128, 64 experts, 12.5%, 28.6.
problems.fix: Reword: 'one preliminary test on Qwen3-30B: 4-bit + 50% pruning (77.6) beat uniform AWQ 2-bit (28.6) at equal size; dynamic 2-bit untested'.

problems.claim: Sec 1 item 1: 'Kimi already ships at 4 bits. Moonshot trained the K2.x experts for INT4, so the full model is 594-595 GB [S6, S9].'
problems.problem: Overgeneralised. K2-Instruct and K2-Instruct-0905 were released in FP8 (1,029 GB) without INT4 QAT; only K2-Thinking, K2.5, K2.6 and K2.7-Code are native INT4. This matters because the ubergarm +7.8% result the dossier relies on is for the non-QAT K2-Instruct.
problems.evidence: HF API moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Instruct usedStorage 1,029,226,387,740 bytes; K2-Thinking card: 'K2 Thinking is a native INT4 quantization model'; K2.6 card: 'adopts the same native int4 quantization method as' K2-Thinking.
problems.fix: Write: 'K2-Thinking and later (K2.5, K2.6, K2.7-Code) ship native INT4 at about 595 GB; K2-Instruct/0905 are FP8 (1,029 GB)'.

verdict: Most of the dossier's cited numbers check out: about 50 load-bearing claims were tested and most match their sources exactly. Seven problems matter beyond detail fixes. (1) Blocker: it says ds4 publishes no streaming speeds, but on 2026-09-06 the maintainer published 128 GB M5 Max measurements. A 753B GLM 5.3 at IQ2_XXS streams at 4.1-5.1 tok/s; a native-MXFP4 DeepSeek Flash at 11.9-19.3 tok/s with 263-300 t/s prefill. This changes the answer to Kevin's 700B question and the dossier's estimates. (2) The pruned DeepSeek row D4 uses the paper's 103 GB, but the published file is 105.6 GiB, so it does not fit; its '130 GB variant' scores belong to an unpruned model. (3) The 288 GB REAP-50 Kimi needs a vLLM fork that is private (404), not published. (4) 'No GGUF/MLX pruned Kimi' is false: Kimi K3 MLX and GGUF builds pruned 50-82% exist, with poor factual recall. (5) The smallest published Kimi K2-family file is 235 GB, not 247-249 GB. (6) DeepSeek V4 Flash checkpoint revisions are mixed up: the AA score of 34 and ds4 Q2 are 0731, while some quant files and fidelity data are from April; the newer V4.1 Flash (AA 39) is missing. (7) The 'try V4.1 Flash Q2 streaming first' recommendation needs 366 GB of disk, more than the dossier's own 358 GB estimate. The remaining items are mis-attributions, wrong baselines and unit slips. The headline 'Kimi itself does not fit usably' still stands, but the 'what works today' and streaming sections need revision before Kevin relies on them.

A3 and every 'active bytes' figure: active bytes per token = active parameters × file-average bits ÷ 8. Instances:

problems.problem: The files keep the non-routed 'spine' at 5-9 bits per weight, plus F32 or F16 routers. Bytes actually read per token are therefore 1.1-2.4× what A3 gives. The routed term is about right; the spine term is badly low. The dossier marks the direction but never quantifies it, and F1, F2, D4 and G1 are off by about 2×.
problems.evidence:
Measured from the GGUF tensor tables, as routed bytes per token + spine bytes per token = total:
- **Kimi K2.6 UD-Q2_K_XL (340.48 GB):** routed 6.90 + spine 8.53 = **15.42 GB**. Spine is 10.55B params at 6.47 bpw; routers alone are 0.66 GB in F32. Dossier: 10.5.
- **K2-Thinking UD-TQ1_0 (246.84 GB):** 4.98 + 7.00 = **11.98 GB**. Dossier: 7.5.
- **V4 Flash ds4 Q2 (86.72 GB):** 1.83 + 7.74 = **9.57 GB**. Attention is Q8 plus F16 compressor and indexer; routed is only 6.49B of 13.3B active. Dossier: 4.0.
- **V4 Flash UD-IQ3_XXS (102.99 GB):** **9.19 GB**. Dossier: 4.7.
- **Qwen3-235B Q2_K_XL:** **9.84 GB**. Dossier: 8.3.
- **Qwen3-235B Q3_K_XL:** **10.81 GB**. Dossier: 9.8.
- **R1 UD-Q2_K_XL:** 6.74 + 10.37 = **17.11 GB**. Dossier: 12.5.
- **R1 UD-IQ1_S:** 4.04 + 10.58 = **14.61 GB**. Dossier: 7.3.
- **GLM-4.7 TQ1_0:** about **11.9 GB**, about 32B active, MTP-only tensors excluded.
- **gpt-oss-120b:** **3.59 GB**. Matches the dossier's 3.55.
problems.fix: Replace A3 with: bytes per token = (routed-pool bytes × k/E) + non-routed bytes, excluding the token embedding. Take both from the GGUF tensor table, not from average bits. Use the measured values listed here in A2-A6 and in every table row.

problems.problem:
The low calibration points come from the byte undercount above. With measured bytes, both M5 Max calibrations give e ≈ 0.61. The chosen e = 0.35-0.46 is below the dossier's own best data. The dossier's gpt-oss estimate (61-79) under-predicts its own measurements (80-105).

Result: in-memory estimates are wrong in both directions.
- F1 and F2 are overstated, because the byte undercount is larger than the e error.
- O1, Q1 and Q2 at short context are understated.
problems.fix: Recalibrate e from measured bytes. Use e = 0.47-0.61 at no more than 2K context, and state that e falls to about 0.43 by 64K, measured on V4 Flash. Restate section 1 as 'about 45-61% at short context'. Recompute the A4 rows with the numbers above.

problems.claim: A5 and A6 use 13.6 GB/s as the upper SSD bandwidth. Section 1: 'Each GB that misses the cache costs about 75 ms.'
problems.problem:
13.6 GB/s is a sequential benchmark peak, and it was measured on a 4 TB unit. Apple's 14.5 GB/s is an 8 TB preproduction unit (FIO, 1 MB requests, QD8). No streaming engine reaches 100% of sequential: the dossier's own best is 78% (SSD-LLaMA).

Kevin's 2 TB drive is unmeasured; smaller capacities usually have less NAND parallelism. On macOS, flash-moe found mmap about 5× slower than pread, so the stock llama.cpp mmap path is far below the 43% lower bound, which was measured on Linux.
problems.evidence:
- Apple newsroom 2026-03-03, footnote 5: preproduction 16-inch M5 Max with an 8 TB SSD, FIO 3.41, 1024 KB request size, 10 GB test file, IO depth 8. Read in part.
- Reviewers: 13.6 GB/s on 4 TB (The Verge via MacDailyNews, search summary) and about 12.7 GB/s on 4 TB (PetaPixel Blackmagic, search summary; page returned 403).
- **Upper bound:** 0.78 × 13.6 = **10.6 GB/s**.
- **Cost per missed GB:** 1/10.6 = **94 ms** to 1/5.85 = **171 ms**, not 75 ms.
- **Stock path:** flash-moe README lists mmap at '-5x' versus pread, which puts stock macOS mmap streaming near 2 GB/s and is consistent with Unsloth's '<1 token/s' guidance.
problems.fix: Use 5.85-10.6 GB/s for purpose-built pread or O_DIRECT streamers, and about 2 GB/s for stock llama.cpp mmap on macOS. Measure the 2 TB drive before any streaming claim: pread of 4-15 MB blocks at QD 1-16, as already planned in G2.

problems.problem:

- **Cache size.** The 88 GB cache must also hold the non-routed weights (9.3 GB for K2.6 Q2), so the experts get about 78.7 GB, or 23.8% of a 331.1 GB pool.

- **K2, K2.6 UD-Q2_K_XL** (routed 6.90, active 15.42, h 0.70-0.80): **2.5-5.8 tok/s**. Best case 0.2×6.90/10.6 + 15.42/377 = 0.171 s. Worst case 0.3×6.90/5.85 + 15.42/288 = 0.407 s.

problems.claim: Section 3b prefill: (336 − 88) GB ÷ 13.6 GB/s = 18.2 s per pass, and compute of 295 tok/s, giving 'about 26 tokens/s' at n = 512 (30K prompt in about 19 minutes) and 'about 128' at n = 4,096 (about 4 minutes). Row K2 repeats these numbers.
problems.problem:
There are two errors.

1. **The cache does not help in prefill.** Each micro-batch scans all experts of layers 1-60 in a fixed cycle. With an LRU-like OS page cache smaller than the 331 GB pool, a cyclic scan gets almost no hits. The full pool is re-read every pass. Subtracting 88 GB would need a pinned, non-LRU cache, which contradicts A7.
2. **Compute ignores attention.** The 295 tok/s figure scales gpt-oss pp2048, measured at 2K context. At a 30K prompt, Kimi's 64-head MLA attention adds 0.6-2× the weight FLOPs.
problems.evidence:
- **One pass, no hits:** 331.1 GB ÷ 10.6 GB/s = 31.2 s, or 56.6 s at 5.85 GB/s.
- **Attention FLOPs:** about 2 × 64 × (576 + 512) = 139K FLOPs per context position per layer in absorbed form, or 41K non-absorbed. At a mean context of 15K: 37-127 GFLOP per token, against 63 GFLOP (2 × 31.7B) for the weights. Compute-bound prefill therefore drops to about 100-185 tok/s.
- **n = 4,096:** 4,096/(31.2 + 13.9) = 91 tok/s best; 4,096/(56.6 + 41) = 42 tok/s worst. A 30K prompt takes **5.5-12 minutes**.
- **n = 512:** **9-16 tok/s**, so a 30K prompt takes 32-57 minutes.
problems.fix: Restate the prefill estimate as 42-91 tok/s at n = 4,096 and 9-16 tok/s at n = 512, and state the no-hit assumption. Note that a pinned cache, as opposed to the OS page cache, would recover at most 88/331 = 27% of the I/O.

problems.claim: A4 (decode held in memory = 215-282 GB/s ÷ active bytes) and A9 ('The sweeps did not capture KV size for Qwen3-235B or GLM-4.6. I reserve 5-10 GiB'). Rows Q1, Q2, G1 and G2 depend on these, including G1's '23-60' tok/s.
problems.problem:
There are two problems.

1. **KV sizes are computable from the configs, and they are larger than the allowance.** The 5-10 GiB allowance covers only about 27-55K tokens for Qwen and 14-28K for GLM. Several fit labels hold only at short context.
2. **A4 ignores KV reads per token.** With GQA, Qwen and GLM read their whole KV cache for every generated token. At 32K this adds 64-104% to the bytes per token, so decode is roughly 40-50% lower than the short-context figure. GLM-4.6/4.7 active parameters are also not unknown: the tensor table gives about 32B.
problems.fix: Add a KV-read term to A4: time = (weights + KV bytes at context) ÷ (e × 614). Replace the 5-10 GiB allowance with the per-token KV sizes above, and state the context length behind each fit label. Set GLM active to about 32B. Note that V4 Flash's compressed KV is why it degrades least with context, which strengthens the dossier's recommendation.

problems.claim: Section 3b, practical recipe step 3: 'For Kevin: if a model larger than RAM is wanted, try ds4's streaming mode with V4.1 Flash Q2 first.'

problems.claim: D4: '103 GB (508B parameters, 1.62 bits average)'; '95.9 GiB + 4 GiB KV at 32K + buffers ≈ 103 GiB', labelled Tight; decode '6.5 GB … up to an assumed 9 GB → 24-43'.
problems.problem: 103 × 10^9 bytes is arithmetically impossible for this recipe, so the paper's '103GB' is almost certainly GiB, like the llama.cpp sizes it compares against. Corrected, the model does not fit under the default Metal ceiling at 32K. Its active bytes are also about 2× the dossier's figure.
problems.evidence:
The paper keeps 192 of 256 experts with top-6 routing, about 32B active; k_b, v_b, token_embd and output at Q8; q_a and q_b at Q6/Q4; kv_a at Q8/Q6/Q5; shared experts at Q6/Q5/Q4; routed experts at IQ1_M/IQ1_S. Source: arXiv 2509.25689, read in full via orx.
- **Minimum possible size:** 490.4B routed × 1.5625/8 (IQ1_S, the smallest llama.cpp type) + 17.1B other × 4.5/8 = 95.8 + 9.6 = **105.4 GB**, which is more than 103 GB. So 103 is GiB, which is 110.6 GB.
- **Fit:** 103 + 4 + 3 = 110 GiB, above the 107.52 GiB ceiling. At the default ceiling, KV room is about 1.5 GiB, or about 12K tokens.
- **Bytes per token:** spine about 10-11 GB (Unsloth R1 IQ1_S's comparable spine is 10.58 GB) + routed 15.3B × 1.56-1.75/8 = 3.0-3.35 GB → 13-14.4 GB, giving **20-29 tok/s**. The paper's '>5 tok/s' on a 256 GB/s Strix Halo is consistent with about 14 GB per token.
problems.fix: Relabel D4 as 'No at 32K under the default ceiling; Tight at about 12K or below, or with a raised wired limit'. Give the file as about 110.6 GB (103 GiB) and decode as 20-29 tok/s, and note that the paper reports sizes in GiB.

problems.claim: Section 3e 'Pruning + streaming': '88 GB cache holds 52% of it, h 0.85-0.90 assumed, routed 7.0 GB, active 10.5 GB → 4.4-11.3 tokens/s'. Row K4: '33% of the 265 GB pool, h 0.70-0.80 assumed → 1.5-4.5'.
problems.problem: Using the cached share of the pruned pool overstates the hit rate. Pruning removes the coldest experts, which carried little traffic. A cache holding 52% of a 50%-pruned pool holds the same hottest 26% of the original experts that it would without pruning, plus the share of redirected traffic that lands on cached experts. The hit rate should be derived from the unpruned routing distribution, not from the fraction of the pruned pool cached. Bytes, e and SSD bandwidth also need correcting.
problems.evidence:
From A7's own curve, the unpruned K2 hit rate at 26% cached is 0.70-0.80; redirected traffic plausibly lifts it to about 0.75-0.85.
- **Pruning + streaming**, with measured Q2 bytes (routed 6.90, active 15.42), 5.85-10.6 GB/s and 288-377 GB/s: **2.9-7.2 tok/s** at h 0.75-0.85, and 2.5-5.8 at h 0.70-0.80. The second is the same as unpruned K2: pruning saves disk, not much decode.
- **K4:** the cache holds about 16.6% of the original experts, so h is about 0.60-0.70. That gives **1.2-2.8 tok/s**, or 1.6-3.9 keeping the dossier's h, with the requantized 17.0 GB active. With the shipped BF16 spine, active is 32.1 GB.
problems.fix: Derive the hit rate for pruned models from the original model's routing trace (G2 can measure this directly). Restate section 3e as about 3-7 tok/s and K4 as about 1.2-3.9 tok/s.

problems.claim: Section 5 and G1: 'Kimi K2.6 INT4 (595 GB) fits, leaving about 45 GB in total, about 5.6 GB per GPU. By A9, one 64K-token sequence needs about 8.1 GiB of MLA cache, so only a few long sequences can run at once.' Also G1/G5: 'vLLM running Kimi K2.6 INT4 at TP8: 0.45-1.1M tokens per GPU-hour (1,000-2,500 tokens/s aggregate)'.
problems.problem:
There are three errors:
- The HBM total is wrong.
- A9's llama.cpp KV format is applied to vLLM.
- Pooling the free memory across GPUs is wrong: under tensor parallelism, MLA's single latent KV head is replicated on every rank.

As a result, only 0-1 sequences of 64K fit, not 'a few'. Aggregate throughput that relies on high concurrency is unverified, so the GPU-hours for G1's INT4 reference and for G5 may be understated.
problems.evidence:
- **HBM:** nvidia-smi reports 81,559 MiB per H100 80GB = 85.5 GB, so 8 GPUs = 684.2 GB, not 640.
- **Free after the model:** 684.2 − 594.5 = 89.7 GB, or 11.2 GB per GPU before CUDA context, NCCL and activations. At vLLM's default gpu_memory_utilization of 0.90, the KV pool is about 21 GB in total (2.7 GB per GPU).
- **KV per token:** vLLM stores the 576-value latent: 576 × 61 × 2 B = 70,272 B per token, on every one of the 8 ranks. SGLang's docs say that without DP attention, the KV cache is duplicated across all TP ranks (search summary).
- **Capacity:** a 64K sequence takes 4.6 GB per GPU, so 0-1 such sequences fit; about 5-12 sequences of 8K tokens fit.
problems.fix: Use 684 GB and per-GPU KV arithmetic. Plan for FP8 KV, `--decode-context-parallel-size`, or SGLang DP attention. Until the one-hour pilot measures aggregate tok/s, budget the vLLM steps of G1 and G5 at 1.5-3× the current figures.

problems.claim: Section 5 disk table: 'Kimi K2.6 2-bit (340.5 GB) alone … about 17 GB' left; 'Kimi 1.8-bit + V4 Flash Q2 … about 24 GB' left. Section 1: 'After the Trash is emptied, the 2-bit (340 GB) … file could be streamed from the SSD.'

Streaming a 340 GB file adds page-cache pressure that pushes other sessions toward swap. With any reasonable free-space floor, the 2-bit Kimi does not fit.
problems.evidence:
- `headroom status` on 2026-10-15: swap 8.4 GB used, 62.5 GB compressed, 'pressure warning'. Kevin's auto-memory records two crashes under concurrency.
- **Margin:** 358 GB free after the Trash − 340.5 GB = 17.5 GB, less than a 20-50 GB swap floor (my assumption).
- **With a 50 GB floor:** 308 GB usable. Only the 235-247 GB 1.8-bit files fit, alone.
problems.fix: Add an explicit free-space floor, for example 50 GB (state it as an assumption), to the disk table. Under that floor the K2.6 Q2 file does not fit, and the only Kimi option is the 235-247 GB 1.8-bit file stored on its own, or an external drive.

problems.claim: A6: time per token = (1 − h) × routed bytes ÷ SSD bandwidth + active bytes ÷ (e × 614). 'SSD reads and compute are assumed not to overlap.'
problems.problem:
Two costs are missing, and the model is never back-tested against the dossier's own Mac streaming data.
- **Copy cost of hits.** If the cache is the OS page cache read through pread, every hit is also a CPU copy from the page cache into a GPU buffer.
- **Per-layer synchronization.** Routing is resolved layer by layer, so there are about 60 serialized I/O and GPU round trips per token.

A back-test on flash-moe fits only when the effective SSD rate is about 3.4 GB/s, and even then A6 is about 20% optimistic.
problems.evidence:
- **Copy cost for K2 Q2 at h = 0.75:** 5.2 GB of hits per token. At an assumed, unmeasured 100-350 GB/s CPU copy rate, that is 15-52 ms per token, or 9-30% of the 171 ms best case.
- **flash-moe back-test** (README, skimmed): M3 Max, 400 GB/s, K = 4, 60 layers, 7.08 MB per expert, about 71% hits from about 35 GB of page cache, 2.41 ms of SSD I/O per layer.
  - Implied SSD traffic: 0.29 × 4 × 7.08 MB × 60 = 0.49 GB per token in 145 ms, which is 3.4 GB/s effective, against the claimed 17.5 GB/s.
  - A6 with 3.4 GB/s plus (1.7 + 5.5) GB at 160 GB/s predicts 190 ms per token (5.3 tok/s). Measured: 4.36 tok/s (229 ms).
problems.fix: Add a hit-copy term (hit bytes ÷ CPU copy bandwidth), or state that the cache must be a pinned Metal buffer, which then counts against the 107.5 GiB ceiling. Add about 20% per-layer overhead, calibrated on flash-moe. Report the back-test in A6.

problems.claim: Section 3e and G5: 'top-8 → 5.8, top-6 → 7.6 (+30%), top-4 → 10.8 tokens/s (+86%)'.

problems.evidence:

verdict:
The headline conclusions hold, and the corrections make them stronger:
- Kimi-class models cannot run usefully on this Mac.
- DeepSeek V4 Flash at about 2 bits is the best model that fits.

Most of the speed and size arithmetic behind them needs fixing.

1. **Bytes per token are undercounted.** A3's average-bits rule misses the high-precision "spine" (attention, shared experts, routers) that every real file keeps at 5-9 bits. Measured from the files' tensor tables:
   - Kimi K2.6 Q2 reads 15.4 GB per token, not 10.5;
   - V4 Flash ds4 reads 9.6 GB, not 4.0.
2. **The decode efficiency is mis-calibrated.** With correct bytes, both M5 Max calibrations give about 61% of 614 GB/s, not 25-46%. Corrected decode:
   - V4 Flash about 30-39 tok/s (dossier 54-71; measured 39.35);
   - gpt-oss-120b 80-105;
   - Qwen3-235B about 29-38 at short context, but 17-23 at 32K, because A4 leaves out KV reads;
   - GLM about 24-32, falling to 12-16 at 32K (dossier 23-60).
3. **The SSD upper bound is optimistic.** 13.6 GB/s is a 4 TB sequential peak; the 2 TB drive is unmeasured; the best engines reach about 78% (10.6 GB/s).
4. **Kimi K2 streaming is slower.** About 2.5-5.8 tok/s with an 88 GB cache (dossier 2.5-7.1), and about 1.4-3 tok/s at today's measured 55 GB of free memory.
5. **Prefill is about 42-91 tok/s, not 128.** The OS page cache gets almost no hits on a cyclic scan of the expert pool.
6. **Pruning plus streaming is about 3-7 tok/s, not 4.4-11.3.** The hit rate must come from the original model's routing.
7. **Two recommendations do not fit:**
   - V4.1 Flash Q2 is 365.7 GB, more than the 358 GB free after the Trash;
   - the pruned 103 GB DeepSeek is really 103 GiB, which is "No" at 32K under the 107.5 GiB ceiling.
8. **Disk headroom is missing.** The plans leave 17-24 GB free on a Mac that is already swapping under memory pressure.
9. **The H100 KV arithmetic is wrong.** The node has 684 GB of HBM, not 640, and MLA's KV cache is copied to every GPU under tensor parallelism. Only 0-1 sequences of 64K fit beside Kimi INT4, so the vLLM GPU-hour estimates for G1 and G5 may be 1.5-3× low.

lens:
Novelty and feasibility of the research gaps (section 4, G1-G5). For each gap I searched orx (alphaXiv), the web, GitHub and Hugging Face for 2025-2026 work that already answers it, then judged whether it can be measured on the 8xH100 host (R570, stock runtimes only) plus the 128 GB Mac within the stated GPU-hours.

Per-gap status:
- G1: PARTLY_DONE.
- G2: OPEN for Kimi K2.
- G3: OPEN (it depends on G1).
- G4: PARTLY_DONE.
- G5: PARTLY_DONE.

Read levels: 'full' means I read the whole text. 'sections' means I fetched the full text but read only the relevant parts. 'report' means I read the alphaXiv summary, not the paper. 'skim' means a WebFetch summary.

problems.claim: Section 3(a) Limits says 'No task benchmarks exist for 1T models below 4 bits'. Row K2 says 'No task benchmarks' for Kimi K2.x at about 2-3 bits. G1 'Why it is open' gives 288 GB (REAP 50% + INT4) as the best measured point.
problems.problem: Task-level results already exist for Kimi K2.5 and K2.6 at about 2 bits, and the checkpoints are public and run on Hopper. The dossier's own source S63, which it lists as read in full, reports a dense INT2 Kimi result that contradicts the 'no task benchmarks' statement.
problems.evidence:
**GSQ** (arXiv 2604.18556, 2026-04-20; full text, Kimi sections read), quantizing routed experts to 2.13 bits per parameter:
- Kimi-K2.5 (Table 3): AIME25 95.33→93.00, GPQA-Diamond 89.29→76.57, LiveCodeBench 61.37→69.37, MATH500 96.68→97.32.
- Kimi-K2.6 with a more diverse calibration mix (Table 6): AIME25 90.00→87.78, GPQA-D 87.21→83.16, MATH500 92.67→93.67.
- AgentBench (Table 14), scores for OS/DB/KG/AlfWorld/WS: base 50/69/57/53/52; Unsloth UD-IQ1_M GGUF (2.4 bits) 40/61/39/41/47; GSQ (2.37 bits) 43/63/45/42/49.
- Runtime (Table 10): GSQ took 24 h on 8×H200 for Kimi-K2.5.

**Released checkpoints:** ISTA-DASLab/Kimi-K2.6-2Bit-GSQ and ISTA-DASLab/Kimi-K2.5-2Bit-GSQ.
- Both created 2026-05-18; 294.0 GB total by the HF API.
- Modified-MIT licence.
- Need vLLM plus the 'humming-kernels' package; the card says 'Hopper (sm_90) or Ampere (sm ≥ 80) GPUs required'.
- URL: https://huggingface.co/ISTA-DASLab/Kimi-K2.6-2Bit-GSQ (card read in full).

**MoESQ** (S63, arXiv 2610.02241, Table 3/6; sections read): 'GSQ Dense INT2 W2A16 2.13 [bits] 77.66 94.22%' on the OpenLLM v1 average for Kimi-K2.5.
problems.fix:
1. Add GSQ (2604.18556) and the ISTA-DASLab checkpoints to S-sources, row K2, section 3(a) and G1 'Why it is open'.
2. Restate the frontier: measured Kimi K2.x points are about 288-294 GB, at 2.13 bits dense (GSQ) or 50% pruning + INT4 (REAP).
3. Note that the GSQ checkpoint runs on the H100 host (vLLM + humming) but has no GGUF or MLX build for the Mac.

problems.claim: G1: 'No published number exists for Kimi beyond 50% pruning ... Pruning beyond 50% is shown only for single-task specialists [S72]'. Hypothesis: a ≤100 GB Kimi K2.6 keeps ≥90% of the INT4 score in knowledge, coding and tool use.
problems.problem: For K2.x the 'no number' claim holds. The sibling Kimi K3, however, already has public pruning results at 50%, 75% and 80-82%, and they predict that G1's general-purpose ≥90% hypothesis fails. Even at 50%, K3 loses about 20-23% of GPQA-Diamond. At 80-82% only code survives. That makes G1 low-novelty and predictably negative as framed.
problems.evidence:
- **nota-ai/Kimi-K3-Nota-Global-Pruned-50** (HF, 2026-08-02; card read). K3 base IFEval 93.72, GPQA-D 86.36. REAP 50%: 87.80 and 66.67. Nota global 50%: 90.02 and 69.19. Maker evaluation.
- **mlx-community/Kimi-K3-mlx-reap160-2bit** (2026-08-01; card read; community report). 82% pruned + 2-bit, 181.2 GB.
  - Code correct; 'The capital of France is' loops.
  - REAP keeps 51.7% of router demand at 160 experts. About 376 experts (≈77% of demand) would be needed.
  - Lowering top_k 16→6 did not help.
- **pipenetwork/Kimi-K3-REAP80-MLX-mxfp4-q8** (2026-07-27; card read; community report). 80% pruned, 350 GB; drifts, and Chinese loops.
- **mgoin/Kimi-K3-pruned75** (2026-07-30; calibration-free): GSM8K 34.42.
- **K2 side, REAP 50%** (S59): knowledge multiple-choice 0.780→0.643, already below 90%.
problems.fix:
1. Cite the K3 evidence in G1 and lower its prior.
2. Either:
   - reframe G1 as a code- or agent-specialist question (a ≤100 GB Kimi K2.6 for coding, with knowledge reported as collateral), which is plausible and still unmeasured; or
   - record G1 as an honest desk exit for general use.
3. If kept, put the K3 numbers in the pre-registration as the prior, and make the 80% top-1 stop rule an explicit expected outcome.

problems.claim: G1 budget is about 90-240 GPU-hours: calibration 11-55, KLD screen of 12 configurations 14-19, task evaluation 53-142, INT4 reference 9-21. Risk: a layer-wise observer is needed.
problems.problem:
The budget leaves out the cost of building competitive ≤2-bit quantized configurations.
- A cheap llama.cpp imatrix k-quant screen is known to understate what 2 bits can reach on Kimi, so a negative screen would not be conclusive.
- A GSQ-class quantizer costs about 192 H200 GPU-hours per configuration.
- The published Kimi REAP calibrations used 8×H200 (1,128 GB). On 8×H100 the 595 GB reference leaves little room.
problems.evidence:
- **GSQ runtime** (2604.18556, Table 10): Kimi-K2.5 took 24 h on 8×H200, i.e. 192 H200 GPU-hours, for one 2-bit model.
- **GSQ vs Unsloth k-quant at equal size:**
  - AgentBench KG: 45 vs 39.
  - Qwen3-4B (Table 13): GSQ-Q2_K 48.34 vs Unsloth-Q2_K 35.01 average.
- **Ex0bit/Kimi-K2.5-PRISM-REAP-530B-A32B** (HF, 2026-02-18; card read): 'Calibration: 512 samples from allenai/tulu-3-sft-mixture, max 2800 tokens'. Hardware: '8x H200 141GB ... used for calibration'.
  - The repo ships reusable saliency scores (calibration/reap_scores_v9_512samples.pt) and a Kimi observer (reap/src/kimi_reap.py).
  - Caution: the scores are pickle .pt files and must be loaded with weights_only=True. They come from an abliterated K2.5 variant.
problems.fix:
1. Add a 'build configurations' line to G1:
   - (a) GGUF imatrix route: CPU-cheap, labelled a lower bound on quality;
   - (b) GSQ route: about 190-250 GPU-hours per configuration, so screen at most 1-2 configurations.
2. Start Stage 1 from the published K2.5 REAP saliency scores and observer code to cut calibration cost.
3. State that a negative result from k-quants alone does not falsify the hypothesis.

problems.claim: Shared assumption: vLLM running Kimi K2.6 INT4 at TP8 gives 0.45-1.1M tokens per GPU-hour (1,000-2,500 tokens/s aggregate). This sets the INT4 reference cost in G1 (9-21 GPU-hours), G2 transcript generation (1.5-3.6) and all of G5 (26-64). G5 risk only notes that 'small KV headroom limits how many requests can run at once'.
problems.problem:
The throughput figure is very likely too high on 8×H100.
- Under TP, the MLA latent KV cache is duplicated on every TP rank. Per-GPU free memory, not the pooled total, sets KV capacity.
- DP-attention would avoid this, but it replicates the attention weights, which likely do not fit next to 1/8 of the INT4 experts in 80 GB.
- With a few GiB per GPU left for KV and about 10K-token thinking outputs, only a handful of sequences can run at once. 1,000-2,500 tokens/s aggregate would need more than 100 tokens/s per sequence.
problems.evidence:
- **SGLang DeepSeek docs** (docs.sglang.ai/references/deepseek; search summary only, not read): 'if you do not use DP attention, KV cache will be duplicated among all TP ranks'.
- **Per-token latent KV** (my arithmetic from the Kimi K2.6 config.json, fetched in full: kv_lora_rank 512, qk_rope_head_dim 64, 61 layers): (512+64)×61×2 bytes = 70,272 bytes.
  - 595 GB = 554 GiB, or 69.3 GiB per GPU under TP8.
  - Assuming about 3 GiB per GPU left for KV: 3 GiB / 70,272 B ≈ 45.8K tokens in total, duplicated on each rank. That is about 4 concurrent 11K-token sequences.
- **Output length:** MoESQ Table 7 (2610.02241) gives a median of 43,810 characters per terminated GPQA-Diamond answer for compressed Kimi-K2.5, roughly 11K tokens.
- The 79.6 GiB usable per H100 is from memory and was not re-verified.
problems.fix:
1. Replace the vLLM K2.6 INT4 throughput with a pilot measurement before registration; until then, carry a 2-6× uncertainty on G1, G2-transcript and G5 budgets.
2. Use FP8 KV cache.
3. Run G5 KLD and routing screens on the 294 GB GSQ 2-bit checkpoint (about 340 GB of HBM free) or on a GGUF with llama.cpp. Keep INT4 only for the final reference.
4. Fix the HBM units: 8×H100 is about 637 GiB usable, not 640 GB, so INT4 leaves about 83 GiB raw before runtime overheads, not 45 GB.

problems.claim: Shared assumption: about 800 items × 2 seeds × about 6,000 generated tokens = 9.6M generated tokens per model setting. This drives every task-evaluation budget in G1, G3, G4 and G5.
problems.problem: 6,000 tokens per item is low for thinking-mode runs of these models on GPQA, AIME and LiveCodeBench, and low-bit quants lengthen chains further [S33]. The reasoning mode is not fixed in the suite. V4 Flash scores very differently across its modes, so the token budget and the comparison both depend on that choice.
problems.evidence:
- **MoESQ** (2610.02241, Table 7): median terminated answer length for Kimi-K2.5 is 43,810 characters on GPQA-Diamond and 42,580 on AIME25. A badly compressed variant reached 105,104 characters, with a 65,536-token cap.
- **V4 Flash model card** (via search summary of the unsloth GGUF page; not read): GPQA-Diamond is 71.2 non-think, 87.4 High and 88.1 Max; MMLU-Pro is 83.0, 86.4 and 86.2.
- **GSQ** evaluated Kimi at temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 (2604.18556, Appendix).
problems.fix:
1. Pin one reasoning mode per model in the suite. Use non-thinking for the cheap tier and one thinking mode for a small subset.
2. Measure tokens per item in the 1-hour pilot.
3. Budget 1.5-2× the current token counts for thinking-mode settings, and report truncation and non-termination separately.

problems.claim: G4: 'Only fidelity metrics exist ... Unsloth's recommended UD-IQ3_XXS has no published metrics'. Reference is Q8_K_XL, 'bit-identical to the official weights'. Five settings, including ds4 Q2.
problems.problem:
**Novelty:** a single-machine fidelity ladder now exists for about 30 V4 Flash quants, including ds4's IQ2XXS file and UD-IQ3_XXS. The open part of G4 is task level only.

**Validity:**
- DeepSeek V4 Flash now has two checkpoints, the original (2026-04-22) and Flash-0731 (2026-07-31). ds4's Q2 target and the measured antirez files are 0731, while Unsloth keeps separate original and -0731 GGUF repos. Mixing them would confound G4.
- The same GGUF gives about 4-5% different perplexity depending on the CUDA kernel path, so H100 results may not transfer to Metal. G4, unlike G3, has no Metal cross-check.
problems.evidence:
- **HF API** (queried 2026-10-15): deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash created 2026-04-22; deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 created 2026-07-31, MIT licence.
- **ds4 MODELS.md** (https://github.com/antirez/ds4/blob/main/docs/MODELS.md; skim): target 'ds4f-q2' is 'DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731', about 81 GiB.
- **AtomicChat/dsv4-eval-artifacts** (HF dataset, 2026-08-03; README and JSONL read in full; maker measurement). Setup: 8×RTX 5090, llama.cpp PR #24162, wikitext-2, context 5632, BF16 reference.
  - antirez IQ2XXS-0731 (86.7 GB): KLD 0.4079, top-1 agreement 78.98%.
  - Unsloth UD-IQ3_XXS-0731 (104.2 GB): KLD 0.2610, top-1 83.46%.
  - Unsloth UD-Q2_K_XL (96.8 GB): KLD 0.3216, top-1 80.92%.
  - The 'lossless' MXFP4 repack itself shows KLD 0.156 and top-1 87.4%.
  - On kernel paths, the README says: 'H100 and H200 are 9.0 ... all take the first path [unpack to BF16]'. Same file: 'RTX 5090 ... 4.5381 | H100 ... 4.3406' perplexity at context 5632.
- **llama.cpp PR #24162 'DeepSeek V4'** (merged 2026-06-29; skim): V4 support, with CUDA, is in mainline. This resolves the G4 risk that CUDA support was unconfirmed. Commenters said antirez GGUFs 'needed naming fixes to load'.
problems.fix:
1. Pin G4 to DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 for every setting: Unsloth -0731 Q8_K_XL as the reference, plus the -0731 ds4 and Unsloth quants.
2. Cite the AtomicChat ladder in place of re-measuring KLD, or reproduce 2-3 of its rows as a check.
3. Add a 100-item Metal (ds4 / llama.cpp) versus H100 agreement subset to G4, as G3 already has.
4. Do a load test of the antirez file on mainline llama.cpp CUDA in the pilot.

problems.claim: G4 hypothesis: ds4 Q2 (80.8 GiB) loses at most 3 points against the official weights; UD-IQ3_XXS loses at most 1 point.
problems.problem: A community model card reported task-level numbers suggesting a mixed-Q2 V4 Flash loses about 8 points. If true, the 3-point hypothesis is likely to fail. The source could not be verified: the repository now returns HTTP 401.
problems.evidence:
Source: Jundot/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-oQ2.5e-mtp (https://huggingface.co/Jundot/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-oQ2.5e-mtp). Undated. Seen only through a search-engine summary; HF API and WebFetch return 401. Unverified community report.

- 90.9 GiB equals the 97.6 GB antirez 'Layers37-42Q4K... IQ2XXS' mixed file listed in antirez/deepseek-v4-gguf (HF API).
problems.fix:
1. Mention this as an unverified prior in G4.
2. Include a non-thinking MMLU-style tier so the result can be compared with the report.
3. Expect the ≤3-point hypothesis to fail for the 2-bit files, and pre-register what follows if it does: for example, recommend UD-IQ3_XXS or Q3 over ds4 Q2 on the Mac.

problems.claim: G5: route each token to 6 or 4 experts instead of 8, with 'gate weights renormalized'. 'Why it is open' cites only flash-moe, KTransformers, ssd-moe and MoBE.
problems.problem:
**Novelty:** reducing top-k is already characterized on many fine-grained MoEs, including two of the dossier's own comparators (V4 Flash and Qwen3-235B), up to 397B. Only the Kimi-specific number is new.

**Validity:** the protocol uses standard renormalization over the reduced set (k2 = k1), which a 2026 paper found to be the worst choice.
- Kimi K2.6 uses sigmoid scoring with norm_topk_prob = true and routed_scaling_factor 2.827, so the gain shifts when k changes.
- Testing only k2 = k1 would overstate the quality cost.
problems.evidence:
- **arXiv 2609.25809** (2026-09-22; sections read). 12 checkpoints across 9 families, including DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, MiniMax-M2.7, Hy3 (295B) and Qwen3-235B. Keeping ⌈2K/3⌉ experts preserves 98.8% on average. V4-Flash k=6→4: 75.69→74.53 average.
- **arXiv 2609.04575** (2026-09-04; alphaXiv report read, not the paper). Qwen3.5-397B, 10→5 experts: MMLU drop is 2.10 with k2 = 5 but 0.55 with k2 = 10 (p = 0.24). The authors call k2 = k1 'consistently the worst choice'.
- **ik_llama.cpp PR #239 'SER'** (merged 2025-03-02; skim; community numbers). DeepSeek R1 IQ3_M wikitext perplexity: 3.1464 at 8 experts, 3.2128 at 6, 3.3133 at 5. Not implemented on Metal.
- **Kimi K2.6 config.json** (HF; read in full): scoring_func sigmoid, norm_topk_prob True, routed_scaling_factor 2.827.
- No Kimi-specific top-k evaluation was found on HF cards (ubergarm, unsloth) or arXiv.
problems.fix:
1. Cite 2609.25809, 2609.04575 and ik_llama SER.
2. Narrow G5's novelty claim to 'first Kimi K2 measurement, plus its interaction with the streaming hit rate'.
3. Pre-register at least two renormalization variants (k2 = k1 and k2 = 8, i.e. anchored to the native k) for top-6 and top-4.
4. Note that vLLM can change num_experts_per_tok by config override, but anchored renormalization needs a Python router patch (no GPU kernel).

problems.claim: G2: 'There is no published routing trace for K2's 384-expert, top-8 routing'. 'Router hooks need Python changes inside a pinned image'. LRU hit rate ≥0.70 at 88 GB, and an A6 model within ±20%.
problems.problem:
**Novelty: confirmed OPEN.** No Kimi K2 trace or hit-rate measurement was found. Published traces and hit rates cover only DeepSeek-V3, Kimi K3, V4 Flash and Qwen.

**Feasibility is better than stated:** stock SGLang already has a per-token expert recorder, so no patch is needed.

**Methodology risk:** a 2026 study shows replay semantics and prompt-template contamination change LRU results by more than G2's ±20% tolerance and can reverse policy rankings.
problems.evidence:
- **SSD-LLaMA** (2609.18110; sections read): streams Kimi-K2.7-Code but reports hit rates only for DeepSeek V4 Flash ('80.1% VRAM hit rate').
- **LMSYS SGLang SSD Expert Pack** (2026-08-29; skim): models were DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi-K3; 'Kimi K2 is not mentioned'.
- **ELDR** (2607.00466) and **ReMoE** (2605.27081): no Kimi mentions in the full text (checked with grep).
- **SGLang source**, python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_distribution.py on main (grep, partial): `expert_distribution_recorder_mode == "per_token"` with a _DetailSinglePassGatherer that stores topk_ids_of_layer.
- **arXiv 2608.07911** (2026-08-04; abstract and introduction read):
  - sequential replay 'inflates LRU by 27.4%' against event-atomic replay;
  - template contamination 'moves the measured early-window effect by 19.4–31.9 percentage points'.
problems.fix:
1. Keep G2 as OPEN and first in order.
2. Use SGLang's --expert-distribution-recorder-mode per_token, with EPLB off so physical IDs equal logical IDs, in place of custom hooks.
3. Pre-register event-atomic replay, diverse prompt templates and the reporting checklist from 2608.07911.
4. Budget transcript generation at realistic throughput (see the KV problem above): about 7-23 GPU-hours rather than 1.5-3.6, still within about 30-50 GPU-hours in total.

problems.claim: G3 compares the best compressed Kimi (at most 105 GB) against DeepSeek V4 Flash ds4 Q2, V4 Flash UD-IQ3_XXS, Qwen3-235B-2507 UD-Q3_K_XL and gpt-oss-120b.
problems.problem:
**Novelty:** OPEN, but the prior is very low (V4 Flash already beats full K2.6 on the index; see also the K3 pruning evidence above), and G3 only runs if G1 produces a candidate.

**Feasibility and validity:** the 'best model that fits natively' list is stale. It leaves out models that ds4 already packages for 96-128 GB Macs. It also does not pin the V4 Flash checkpoint (original or 0731).
problems.evidence:
- **ds4 MODELS.md** (skim): glm53-q2 (GLM 5.3 Flash) 90 GiB; qwen38-q4k (Qwen3.8 Flash Next) 69.74 GiB resident; ds4f-q2 is Flash 0731.
- The dossier itself lists GLM-5.3-Flash (320B / 18B active, 93-109 GB, MIT) as fitting but without quality data.
problems.fix:
1. Make G3 strictly conditional on a G1 Stage-1 pass.
2. Add GLM-5.3-Flash ds4 Q2 and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next to the comparator set.
3. Pin V4 Flash to 0731.
4. Consider replacing G3 with a cheaper desk comparison, using the published GSQ AgentBench and Artificial Analysis numbers, unless G1 passes.

problems.claim: Section 5 H100 host: 'driver R570, CUDA 12.8 or lower'. Runtimes listed as stock: vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp CUDA, ik_llama.cpp, EXL3, KTransformers.
problems.problem:
Two runtime facts affect gap feasibility and were not recorded.
1. Current vLLM images are CUDA 13. Their documentation says compatibility mode supports R570 host drivers on datacenter GPUs, so 'CUDA ≤12.8' need not pin the host to an old vLLM.
2. The only Kimi 2-bit checkpoint with task results (GSQ) needs the third-party 'humming-kernels' package. Its status under 'stock runtimes only' needs a decision.
problems.evidence:
- **vLLM Docker docs** (https://docs.vllm.ai/deployment/docker.html, latest; skim): images 'come with CUDA compatibility libraries pre-installed'. For CUDA 13 images, compatibility mode supports 'R535 and R570 host drivers' on 'select professional and datacenter NVIDIA GPUs'; enabled with VLLM_ENABLE_CUDA_COMPATIBILITY=1.
- **ISTA-DASLab/Kimi-K2.6-2Bit-GSQ card:** 'Loading this checkpoint requires vLLM plus the humming MoE kernels (pip install humming-kernels)'.
problems.fix:

verdict:
Three of the five gaps are already partly answered by 2026 work the dossier missed. The GPU-hour budgets for G1 and G5, and the token assumption behind every budget, are probably too low.

- **G1, PARTLY_DONE.**
  - Already done:
    - GSQ (2604.18556) published task results for Kimi K2.5 and K2.6 at 2.13 bits (K2.6: GPQA-D 87.21→83.16), and the 294 GB checkpoints are public and run on Hopper.
    - REAP 50% + INT4 is measured.
    - Kimi K3 pruning at 50%, 75% and 80-82% (Nota card, REAP-160/179 MLX builds) shows general knowledge collapsing beyond 50%.
  - What remains: no Kimi K2.x at ≤100 GB has been measured. With this prior, the ≥90% general-purpose hypothesis is very likely false.
  - Better framing: a code-specialist ≤100 GB Kimi, or an honest desk exit for general use.
  - Feasibility:
    - A Stage-1 GGUF screen is cheap but not conclusive.
    - A competitive 2-bit quantizer costs about 192 H200 GPU-hours per configuration.
    - The 595 GB INT4 reference is limited by duplicated MLA KV on 8×H100.
    - So the program likely exceeds 240 GPU-hours. The biggest blocker is HBM/KV headroom plus quantizer cost.
    - Disk (20 TB) and licence (modified MIT) are fine.
- **G2, OPEN for Kimi K2.**
  - Published traces and hit rates cover only DeepSeek-V3, Kimi K3, V4 Flash and Qwen.
  - Feasible at about 15-50 GPU-hours with stock SGLang's per_token expert recorder, so no patch is needed.
  - Biggest blockers: Mac disk (a 336-340 GB replay file leaves about 17 GB free) and memory contention.
  - The protocol must adopt event-atomic replay and diverse prompt templates (2608.07911).
- **G3, OPEN.**
  - Conditional on G1, with a low prior.
  - The comparator list is stale (missing GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and V4 Flash 0731).
  - Not worth GPU-hours unless G1 Stage 1 passes.
- **G4, PARTLY_DONE.**
  - A single-machine fidelity ladder for about 30 V4-Flash-0731 quants exists (AtomicChat; antirez IQ2XXS KLD 0.408, top-1 78.98%).
  - A task-level result exists only in an unverifiable community card (about −8 points for a 90.9 GiB mixed Q2, thinking off).
  - Feasible at 20-60 GPU-hours once these are fixed:
    - pin the 0731 checkpoint;
    - fix the reasoning mode;
    - add an H100-vs-Metal agreement check (perplexity differs about 4-5% by CUDA kernel path).
  - llama.cpp CUDA support is now confirmed (PR #24162, merged 2026-06-29). antirez files may need naming fixes to load.
- **G5, PARTLY_DONE.**
  - Reducing top-k is characterized on 9-12 fine-grained MoEs up to 397B, including V4 Flash and Qwen3-235B: 2/3 of the experts keeps 98.8%, and the renormalization choice matters.
  - It has not been measured on Kimi K2.
  - The 'renormalized' protocol uses the variant shown to be worst, so add anchored renormalization.
  - The 30-70 GPU-hour budget is likely 2-6× low on INT4 TP8. Run the screen on the GSQ 2-bit checkpoint or a GGUF instead.

**Order:** G2 first, then G4 with the 0731 pin, then G5 with corrected renormalization. Run G1 only in its reframed form, and G3 only if G1 passes.
